preview.instructions:
You write the questions that will close the most uncertainty in the fewest asks.

You are not a question-asking machine. Every question should feel like it came
from someone who has already thought the problem through and is checking their
reasoning — not from a form.

Every question names the coverage `dimension` it serves. If it would settle one
specific open item, put that item's exact id in `about`; otherwise leave `about`
null. A question about something nobody has mentioned at all is often…

questions.text: What type of product or service will this tool analyze for gaps in knowledge?
questions.rationale: The framework to identify gaps is specific to the product domain; we cannot define what categories of gaps matter without knowing whether we're analyzing software, hardware, services, or market positioning.

options.label: Software/SaaS product
options.elaboration: Features, capabilities, behavior, APIs, integrations, pricing, terms of service
options.commits: Framework will categorize gaps across software-specific dimensions: feature completeness, behavioral consistency, integration scope, pricing clarity, and support boundaries

options.label: Hardware/Physical product
options.elaboration: Specifications, materials, manufacturing, durability, safety, environmental impact
options.commits: Framework will categorize gaps across product-specific dimensions: specification completeness, safety and regulatory clarity, manufacturing process definition, and sustainability claims

options.label: Service offering
options.elaboration: Delivery scope, method, service level agreements, pricing, support, contingencies
options.commits: Framework will categorize gaps across service-specific dimensions: scope clarity, delivery method definition, SLA specification, support boundaries, and contingency planning

options.label: Market positioning and go-to-market
options.elaboration: Value proposition, messaging, customer segmentation, competitive positioning, pricing strategy
options.commits: Framework will categorize gaps across market-specific dimensions: customer clarity, value proposition definition, differentiation, and pricing rationale

questions.text: Who will use this tool and what problem are they solving?
questions.rationale: Different user roles need different information and care about different gaps; understanding who is asking and why determines what framework will actually be useful to them.

options.label: Product managers documenting product definition
options.commits: Tool must work with incomplete/ambiguous input and help surface hidden thinking gaps; output becomes a specification

options.label: Go-to-market teams validating marketing claims
options.commits: Tool must identify and flag gaps between what marketing says and what the product actually does; output exposes inconsistencies

options.label: Cross-functional teams aligning on shared understanding
options.commits: Tool must surface disagreements between functions and explain gaps in language non-specialists understand

options.label: Support and documentation teams ensuring coverage
options.commits: Tool must work from end-user perspective and identify what customers need to know or do that isn't documented

questions.text: What are your timeline and operating constraints?
questions.rationale: Timeline and technical boundaries determine whether the framework can be a simple checklist, a structured interactive questionnaire, or a sophisticated AI-assisted system.

options.label: MVP needed in 1-2 weeks
options.commits: Framework must be simple enough to operate without custom tooling; likely a static checklist or questionnaire

options.label: 2-4 weeks available
options.commits: Can build interactive tooling with conditional logic and branching; framework can be moderately detailed and context-aware

options.label: Several weeks to months
options.commits: Can build a sophisticated interactive system, possibly with AI assistance; framework can be nuanced and domain-specific without implementation worry

options.label: Must run offline or in air-gapped environment
options.commits: Cannot depend on cloud APIs or external services; framework and tool must be entirely self-contained and portable

questions.text: How will you know when this tool is working and delivering value?
questions.rationale: The success criteria clarifies which gaps matter most and what the tool should prioritize, shaping the framework design and interaction model.

options.label: Gaps are surfaced early, team manually fills them before build/launch
options.commits: You're accepting that the tool's value is early discovery, not creating ongoing reference material; success is measured by gaps caught before product work begins

options.label: Tool becomes the living source of truth for product definition
options.commits: You're accepting ongoing maintenance burden and that the tool must support version control, collaboration, and team workflows; success is team adoption and continued use

options.label: Speeds up time-to-market by catching gaps during discovery
options.commits: You're accepting that ROI is comparative and requires a baseline; you'll need to measure this against your previous process to prove value

options.label: Produces executive and stakeholder confidence in product definition
options.commits: You're accepting that gaps must be explained in business and strategic terms, not just technical ones; success is stakeholder buy-in, not complete documentation
